sections.text: This program is for current Princeton MOL rising seniors (doing lab theses) and Princeton rising sophomores, juniors, and seniors working with LSI faculty. You do not need to apply . The MOL department will send out information in February. LSI students contact Ben Zhang, xzhang2@princeton.edu , with questions.

sections.heading: Program Overview
sections.text: Faculty Adviser: Dr. Zemer Gitai Link sends email

sections.heading: For current MOL juniors:
sections.text: Molecular Biology juniors planning to write a laboratory-based senior thesis are invited to participate in the Summer Undergraduate Research Program. No application is necessary. Students interested in participating should inform their adviser. Molecular Biology juniors participating in the program are provided with a stipend but are responsible for their own housing and travel.

sections.heading: For current MOL juniors:
sections.text: Employment outside the research program is permissible only during evening hours or weekends and should not interfere with research activities. Students may take non-credit-bearing courses, such as MCAT review courses or EMT training, but they cannot enroll in a credit-bearing course (one that would fulfill a requirement or count for academic credit at Princeton) while participating in SURP.

sections.heading: For current MOL juniors:
sections.text: Rising sophomores and juniors are also welcome to participate if they are able to secure a position and funding in an affiliated laboratory. There is no formal mechanism for placing rising sophomores and juniors in laboratories; students are responsible for contacting faculty members directly about potential research opportunities. One possible funding source for sophomores and juniors is the Office of Undergraduate Research OURSIP Link is external program. The Summer 2027 funding application through OURSIP opens January 25, 2027 and the deadline will be March 22, 2027.

sections.heading: For other students working with LSI faculty:
sections.text: Students are responsible for finding a research lab in which to work over the summer. To be eligible for funding through the Lewis-Sigler Institute, students must work in the lab of an LSI faculty member Link is external , and the lab must be located on the Princeton University campus. Eligible students will receive a contract from the QCB program administrator in February. The contract must be signed by both the student and the faculty member to confirm participation and is typically due in mid-March.

sections.text: Currently enrolled Princeton undergraduate students can apply for summer funding to do research by creating an application in SAFE and searching for funding opportunities. Princeton students are encouraged to participate in the PNI Summer Internship Program activities.

Princeton undergraduates can apply for funding, provided by the University, to participate in a summer research opportunity in a PNI faculty lab. You should search for funding opportunities in SAFE Link is external, Link opens in new window (to include Re-Match, Global Health, OURSIP, and others). Prior to applying for funding, you can reach out to individual PNI faculty, based on your research interest, to see if they have availability in their lab for the summer. It is important that you have secured a faculty member’s agreement to conduct summer research in their lab before you apply for funding. After you have secured a faculty lab assignment and university funding, you are welcome to participate with the NEU visiting Summer Internship Program (attend faculty talks, workshops, Matlab, webinars, etc.).

sections.heading: Funding Options
sections.text:
Funding for internships may be available through one of the sources listed below. Support must be in place for your summer opportunity. In some cases, opportunities will also offer funding for materials for your project. Please contact the Office of Undergraduate Research at our@princeton.edu regarding funding requirements and deadlines.
S.A.F.E. (Student Activity Funding Engine) Link is external, Link opens in new window - The various University funding resources are posted on the S.A.F.E. website, each opportunity specifying the type of project it will support. Be careful to choose opportunities listing guidelines that are a good fit with your project. A single application is required; you will then indicate all of the opportunities for which you are applying for that application. The coordinators of the opportunities will work together to decide whether your application will be funded and, if accepted, the total amount of the award you will receive. Do not submit more than one application/project proposal or you will jeopardize your eligibility for support. Note: if you apply for OUR Senior Thesis Research Funding (STRF) for the summer cycle, you must also select NEU and/or any other departmental or programmatic funds for which you are eligible. Outside Resources - Some online diligence may produce a source of funding for your internship. The National Science Foundation (NSF) is an example. Such opportunities tend to be few but may be worth the time spent to identify them and apply. A discussion with your faculty mentor may help you identify funding resources used by prior undergraduates in your lab. Faculty Support - In some instances, your faculty mentor may be able to provide an educational stipend. In such cases, written approval of that agreement should be sent via e-mail to the Undergraduate Administrator by your faculty mentor.

sections.text: The HMEI Climate and Environmental Sciences and Engineering Graduate Fellowship Program (HMEI-CESEn) enables Ph.D. candidates in science, engineering, and other academic disciplines to add an environmental and/or climate-focused science/engineering dimension to their doctoral research. Admission to the program is by competitive application taken annually in the spring semester.
Awarded students receive half support (tuition and stipend) from HMEI for two years and are expected to complete the requirements of the program. ( See below for academic requirements .)

HMEI-CESEn Fellows also receive a $3,500 award to support their graduate research. HMEI-CESEn students may apply for teaching assistantships with the Program in Environmental Studies (with approval from their adviser).

Students supported by the HMEI-CESEn Fellowship are expected to complete the following program requirements:
Complete two (2) HMEI (ENV) graduate courses on climate/environment. A list of courses is available here . Other courses may be approved on a case-by-case basis including most classes offered in AOS, GEO, CEE, and EEB at the graduate level. Students wishing to pursue alternative courses to fulfill the requirement must receive approval from the CESEn Faculty Program Coordinator. Note: A single course, completed prior to accepting the Fellowship, may count towards the two-class requirement. To fulfill this requirements, courses must be taken for a grade or P/D/F. Audited courses do not qualify. Produce an advanced climate/environmental science and engineering research paper. This paper must be the outcome of research pursued with the student’s HMEI-CESEn adviser, and in many cases as joint research with the dissertation adviser, with the aim for Fellows to publish research papers in peer-reviewed journals on a new topics/in new fields connected to environmental sciences and engineering. There is an expectation that research conducted as an HMEI-CESEn Fellow will be developed as a chapter of the student’s dissertation. Note: Research supported by the CESEn Fellowship should take place in the two academic years following the award. Attend HMEI Faculty Seminars . HMEI Faculty Seminars are held monthly during the fall and spring semesters.

Princeton graduate students (post-generals) are eligible to apply for the HMEI-CESEn Fellowship. Applicants must demonstrate a strong interest in pursuing environment-related research and identify an HMEI-CESEn adviser in addition to their thesis adviser from their home department. The HMEI-CESEn adviser is expected to be included on the student’s dissertation committee.
DCE students are not eligible and will not be considered.

Selection into the HMEI-CESEn program is determined by competitive application each spring. Criteria for selection include a strong academic record, a well thought-out research plan, and engagement of the student’s departmental thesis adviser in the research plan.

To apply, HMEI-CESEn Fellowship candidates are required to submit a completed application form and to develop a 2 page research proposal in cooperation with their thesis adviser. Recommendations from the applicant’s current Ph.D. adviser and the proposed HMEI-CESEn adviser are required components of the application package.
View the HMEI-CESEn Program Application page for more information and application deadlines.

sections.heading: Faculty & Academic Professional Staff
sections.text: The Department of Molecular Biology at Princeton University has an occasional curricular need for lecturers to teach, co-teach, or lead precepts in areas such as molecular biology, cell and developmental biology, biochemistry, and genetics, and accepts applications in advance in the event the occasion arises where such lecturers are needed. Any appointments and duty time are subject to enrollments and may be for one or two semesters during the 2026-2027 academic year. Positions would have an expected start date of September 1, 2026, or January 16, 2027. Individuals should possess a Ph.D. in  Molecular Biology or related field and have experience with teaching at the undergraduate level.  Successful candidates will attend weekly lectures, be present during lab, lead weekly discussions, hold regular office hours, meet with the course instructor(s), and assist in exam writing and grading as it applies to the course being taught. Princeton University is especially interested in qualified candidates who can contribute, through their research, teaching, and/or service, to the diversity and excellence of our academic community.

sections.heading: Faculty & Academic Professional Staff
sections.text: If you are interested in searching among opportunities or applying for a faculty or academic professional staff position, please apply through Princeton University's Interfolio page Link is external . To find MolBio specific offerings, select “Molecular Biology” from the “Filter by Unit” dropdown.

sections.heading: Administrative or Research Staff
sections.text: If you are interested in searching among opportunities or applying for an administrative or research staff position, please apply through the Careers at Princeton Site (CAPS) Link is external . To find MolBio specific offerings, type “Molecular Biology” in the “Search by keyword” field.

sections.text: Most students elect to work in an adviser's laboratory (lab-based thesis). The student works independently but under supervision to plan and conduct experiments to advance scientific knowledge. Students are expected to analyze and interpret critically the results of experiments, to use their results to guide subsequent experiments, and to integrate knowledge from various sources. Students who choose a lab thesis are strongly encouraged (but not required) to participate in our summer research program after their junior year.

Each thesis is read and graded by the student's adviser and two additional faculty members. In addition to submitting the thesis document, students are required to present their work to the two non-adviser thesis readers in a 30-minute oral exam. The adviser and readers use a grading rubric for each component. There are separate rubrics for the oral exam, lab thesis, non-lab thesis, and computational thesis.
If you need an extension, you must contact Professor Fred Hughson.

Extensions beyond the University’s submission deadline (April 26) can only be granted by your college Dean with the approval of the Undergraduate Studies Committee. Any extensions past the Dean’s date (May 4) must be approved by the Office of the Dean of Undergraduate Students.

sections.text: It is now possible for the University to note a milestone credit on the transcript for students who have successfully completed a summer internship related to their home department with proper approval. The Department of Molecular Biology will consider requests for academic credit which will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis by the Director of Undergraduate Studies. The Department criteria is that the internship must be at least six weeks long, and related to molecular biology. The Summer Undergraduate Internship Milestone Credit application is accessible via TigerHub Link is external .

At the end of the internship, students will submit a 1-2 page paper to the department as well as a letter from the company detailing responsibilities and overall performance. After this is approved, the Registrar’s Office will note the milestone credit on the transcript. [ Please note that this credit does not count toward the 33-34 University required courses toward graduation .]

The summer internship milestone credit program will be made available to sophomores who are in the process of declaring Molecular Biology as a major in the fall of their junior year, subject to the discretion of the Department using the criteria outlined above. Please note that the program will not be available to first year students.

sections.heading: Available Funding
sections.text: Princeton Neuroscience Institute has received several generous donations from alumni for undergraduate research senior thesis awards. These research awards can be used for purchasing research materials and supplies, human subject participant fees, publication-related costs, and scans. Please review the funding opportunity information in SAFE for a full list of permitted uses of the funds. Research awards cannot be used as summer internship funding for food, housing, or summer transportation.

sections.heading: Available Funding
sections.text: Applications should be submitted through SAFE Link is external . Please contact neu-undergrad@princeton.edu if you have any questions.

sections.heading: Eligibility & Application Requirements
sections.text: Students in the Neuroscience Major are eligible to apply for PNI senior thesis awards during the Spring semester of Junior year. Award applications should include: dates of the project, description of research/project summary, a budget showing how the student plans to use the funds, who the student intends to work with/lab in which they plan to work, and an adviser evaluation. All applicants will be notified by email.
